sentence_stem: If you practise football every day,
correct_completion: you will play better than before.
full_sentence: If you practise football every day, you will play better than before.
acceptable_variants: you will get better every week.
your team will win more games.

options.why_wrong: 'If' introduces a condition about the future, so the main clause must describe a future result, not a past event.

options.text: you will play better than before.
so you became a good player.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result that has already happened, which does not fit a conditional clause describing a future result.
This describes an object and does not give the result of practising every day.

grammar_focus: First conditional with comparative 'better than before'
explanation: After 'if' with a present tense, the main clause uses 'will' to describe the future result. Spanish speakers may be tempted to use a past form here, so keep the result clause in the future.
translation: Si practicas fútbol todos los días, jugarás mejor que antes.
